steps.title: Palomino
steps.body: Palomino Fino is about 95% of the vineyards. It's neutral, low in acidity and sugar, giving base wines of about 11 to 12.5%. Its neutrality is a strength: Sherry's flavours come from ageing, flor and oxygen, not from the grape.

steps.title: Sweet grapes
steps.body: Pedro Ximénez, PX, and Moscatel are used for sweet wines and for sweetening blends. They're often dried in the sun on mats, asoleo, for one to three weeks, becoming almost raisins. Much PX comes from nearby Montilla-Moriles, which is allowed in Sherry. Fermentation is stopped early by fortification, keeping huge sugar levels.

steps.prompt: Match each grape to its use.

steps.body: Pedro Ximénez is one of the sweetest wines in the world, often over 400 g/l of sugar. Pour it over vanilla ice cream.

steps.prompt: Why is Palomino ideal for Sherry?
options: Its neutrality lets ageing create the flavours
steps.explanation: Flor and oxygen write the flavour.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Palomino, about 95%, gives neutral base wines
PX and Moscatel are dried in the sun for sweet wines
Sherry's flavour comes from ageing, not the grape
